songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: Stellar Cryptical‑Drums‑Other One suite with soaring New Speedway Boogie
ai_show_review.blurb: The show shines on the epic Cryptical → Drums → The Other One sequence and a bright acoustic set that culminates in New Speedway Boogie. Jerry’s vocals are inspired, Bob’s banter is memorable, and the second‑set jams stay tight despite a few rough moments.
ai_show_review.review: June 7, 1970 at Fillmore West captures the Dead in a relaxed yet adventurous mood. The first set rolls through acoustic gems—Don’t Ease Me In, Friend of the Devil and a sparkling New Speedway Boogie where Garcia’s voice soars (even if it shows a hint of strain) and his pedal‑steel adds extra color. The second set is the real highlight: a seamless Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → The Other One suite that many reviewers call “epic” and “fabulous,” with drummers building an atmospheric tension that erupts into a focused, intense Other One. Good Lovin’ gets a nice double‑jam treatment, and Casey Jones closes the night on a high note. Recording-wise the Hollister soundboard (gd70-06-07.sbd.hollister.98.sbeok.shnf) offers clear, well‑balanced audio despite a heavy bass tilt and a splice glitch in Cumberland Blues, while an audience tape from Bear is praised for crystal‑clear fidelity. Overall the performance is consistently praised across all sources, making this show a must‑listen for fans of early‑70s improvisation.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: All three recordings are marked positive; reviewers repeatedly call the Cryptical‑Drums‑Other One suite 'epic', 'fabulous' and highlight New Speedway Boogie, Cumberland Blues and other jams as standout. No consistent negative commentary on playing quality appears, so a strong positive adjustment is applied.

best_recording.reason: Clear soundboard capture with superb acoustic set and the legendary Cryptical‑Drums‑Other One suite, despite minor bass heaviness.

key_highlights: Epic Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → The Other One sequence
Soaring New Speedway Boogie that showcases Garcia’s vocal and pedal‑steel work
Strong acoustic opening with tight interplay and Bob’s engaging banter
Good soundboard quality overall; Bear audience tape noted as crystal clear

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s voice shines on New Speedway Boogie (though a bit strained) and his pedal‑steel adds texture to the acoustic numbers; guitar work is consistently praised across recordings.
band_performance.Phil: Generally solid bass foundation with only occasional raggedness noted on Silver Threads, otherwise no major issues.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s lead vocals on Cosmic Charlie receive positive nods; his crowd banter is remembered fondly and adds character to the set.
band_performance.Mickey: Drummers deliver atmospheric interludes between Cryptical and The Other One, described as fabulous with a nice build‑up; intensity peaks during the Other One sequence.
